items.name: Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon on November 18, bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work and science workflows. It is rolling out in the Gemini API, Gemini for business and paid Gemini app plans.
items.plain: A fast Google AI for coding, analysis and business work that gives teams high-end help without waiting on the slowest top-tier models.

items.name: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on November 17, with Astra as its new frontier model for hard, long-running projects and Sol as the suggested everyday default. Both are available in the OpenAI API, ChatGPT and Codex.
items.plain: OpenAI's newest work AI pair — a top model for hard projects and a cheaper everyday model — for professional and development work.

items.name: Qwen4-Max
items.summary: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on November 16, a near-frontier flagship model for long-horizon and professional-domain agent work with text, image and video input. It is available through QwenCloud, QwenWork, QwenStudio and OpenRouter; there are no open weights for this model.
items.plain: Alibaba's flagship AI for multi-step agent and professional work, giving businesses a strong non-US option for automated workflows.

items.name: Tencent Hy4
items.summary: Tencent published the full Hy4 open weights on November 20, its 770B-parameter multimodal flagship with vision and computer use, alongside FP8 and pre-trained base variants on Hugging Face, ModelScope and GitCode. The weights are released under the Tencent Hy License v1.0, with extra terms for very large API providers.
items.plain: A very large open AI that businesses can download and run themselves for chat, vision and computer-use tasks instead of only renting it.

items.name: MAI Code 2
items.summary: Microsoft launched MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash at Ignite on November 17, a family of agentic coding models for deep debugging, multi-file changes and repository-wide reasoning. Both models are available in GitHub Copilot, with Flash aimed at high-volume routine fixes and edits.
items.plain: Microsoft's coding AI inside GitHub Copilot that helps development teams debug, change and ship software faster at lower cost.
